RETRAUCI - Justification of the regional AIS severity cutoff (>= 4 vs >= 3)

2026-11-09

Purpose

Each anatomical region is coded as a Yes/No severity variable from its regional AIS (0-6). The cutoff used so far was AIS >= 3; this document looks at how 30-day mortality changes with the regional AIS level in each region, to help decide whether AIS >= 3 or AIS >= 4 is a better definition of “severe”.

All years present in the registry export are used (no split by year), and patients are analysed region by region, without taking the injuries in the other regions into account.

1. Data

The cohort is built with the preprocessing code of ultimate_validation_preprocessing.Rmd (all code before the heading “Preprocessed cohort” is executed).

2. Mortality by AIS level in each region

If AIS 4 is a better cutoff than AIS 3, mortality should rise clearly between 3 and 4 and not between 2 and 3. The table shows deaths / patients (30-day mortality) at each AIS level; the figure shows the same with 95% Wilson confidence intervals (levels with fewer than 10 patients are not drawn). Dotted lines mark the two candidate cutoffs.

Mortality by AIS level, alone or together with another region

Same figure, now with six lines per panel. In each panel (region) the patients injured in that region (AIS 1-6) are split in these groups:

  • Only this region: no other region has any injury (AIS 0 in the other five).
  • **+ Head, + Upper extremity, + Thorax, + Abdomen, + Lower extremity,
    • External**: the other region named has an injury (AIS >= 1), whatever its severity and whatever happens in the remaining regions.

The “+” groups overlap: a patient with injuries in the region plus head and thorax appears in both the “+ Head” and the “+ Thorax” lines. Colours are the same for the same region in every panel. Levels with fewer than 10 patients in a group are not drawn, the lines are shifted slightly horizontally so that the confidence intervals do not overlap, and the y axis is the same in all panels. AIS 0 is not drawn because the lines refer to patients injured in the region.

3. Mortality by number of regions and by highest AIS (any region)

Here the region is not taken into account: each patient is described by how many of the six regions are injured, and by the highest AIS among the six regions. All years and all patients are used. A region counts as injured when its AIS is 1 or more. The six regions are head, upper extremity, thorax, abdomen, lower extremity (including pelvis) and external. Patients with AIS 0 in all six regions (no injury recorded in any of them) are shown in the tables but not in the figures; their meaning is doubtful, since an empty AIS is coded as 0.
